text:
maria (support): Hey — customer on account 4765 is seeing a 401 when calling our streaming /v1/chat/stream endpoint from their on-prem infra. They provided a short curl but it never upgrades to a stream. Request id from our logs: req-20260315-9f7a. Can someone help craft a minimal curl repro they can run and verify headers?

jonah (eng): Thanks — can you paste the exact curl they ran? 401 usually auth header mismatch or token scoped to a different region. For streaming make sure to use -N and Accept: text/event-stream, and don't set Content-Length. Also include the full Authorization header value when testing.

maria (support): Here's what the customer tried (redacted token):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/chat/stream \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"stream":true}'
```
They said it immediately returns HTTP/1.1 401 and body {"error":"unauthorized"}. Our logs show the same request id.

jonah (eng): Two quick repro variants to try. First, a simple non-streaming call to confirm token validity: a single POST to /v1/chat with the same body (no stream flag). If that passes then it's streaming-specific. Second, the canonical streaming curl I use locally — should reproduce the SSE connection and surface any auth failure in headers:

```
# canonical streaming repro
curl -v -N https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/chat/stream \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"test stream"}],"stream":true}'
```

Notes: -N disables buffering so curl prints events as they arrive. Keep -v for header/handshake details. If you see 401 in the response headers, check that the token is exact and not wrapped/URL-encoded. Also confirm the token is valid for the region (us-west-2).

ingrid (customer): I pasted that exact streaming curl and got the same 401. Non-streaming /v1/chat works fine for us. Token was generated from the console in us-west-2.

jonah (eng): Ok that isolates it to streaming behavior. Two possibilities: 1) a proxy in their on-prem path is stripping Authorization on upgrade requests, 2) our edge rejects the upgrade if certain headers are present. Can you ask customer to run curl -v and paste the handshake section (we just need the request/response headers)? Example chunk of interest:

```
> POST /v1/chat/stream HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood-inference.example
> Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_TOKEN
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Content-Type: application/json
> Content-Length: 123

< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: req-20260315-9f7a
```
If they see Authorization missing in the outgoing request (curl shows it in the > lines) but the response is 401 and our edge logs show no auth header, then it's a proxy removing it.

maria (support): Customer pasted the -v output. They do show Authorization in the request line. Our edge logs show the auth header present but our auth service returns 401 with reason "token_scope_mismatch". Token was created from the console with limited scopes (embedding-only) — customer says they thought API keys are global.

infra-bot: debug-bundle created: dbg-92a7 (expires in 7 days). Uploaded logs: /debugs/dbg-92a7/req-20260315-9f7a-logs.txt

jonah (eng): Good catch — that explains it. Streaming endpoint requires the chat generation scope (scope: chat.generate). The console flow should warn about scopes — we'll add a doc note. For the immediate fix, customer needs to create a key with chat.generate scope or use their org service key.

ingrid (customer): Ok will create a new key and try. If it's still failing I'll paste the debug bundle. Thanks for the quick triage. :pray:

maria (support): One more thing for support to provide back to customer — the minimal validated curl we can give them (replace token):
```
curl -N -v https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/chat/stream \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_CHAT_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"confirm stream"}],"stream":true}'
```

Also remind them to avoid adding upstream proxies that strip Authorization on upgrade/streaming requests.

jonah (eng): I'll follow up with a short docs PR to call out scope differences and streaming header gotchas. Leave a note to escalate to infra if we see tokens with correct scope still 401-ing (possible edge bug).

maria (support): Marking this thread resolved for now. If customer returns with same request id I will reopen with the debug bundle link. :white_check_mark:
